A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Tiled Diffusion and have readable text, equations, figures, and tables. Neither includes the separately referenced supplementary document or an appendix. This limits verification of the additional supplemental analyses mentioned in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original generated-image comparisons, evaluation using 1,000 LAION captions, constraint ablations, and scalability results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original quantitative evaluation, ablations, scalability plots, and qualitative image-generation results.

M1.justification: The tiling and similarity constraints, round-robin selection, latent rotation, decoding and cropping, and image-to-image procedure remain unchanged. The new supplementary references do not specify a method modification.

E1.justification: The visible LAION evaluation, three tiling scenarios, and image, texture, and panorama applications are retained. V2 newly mentions example-based texture-synthesis evaluation in the separate supplement, but the supplied PDFs cannot establish whether this extends the earlier task coverage.

E2.justification: AT, STI, VT2I, and Swapped VT2I retain the same participation in the displayed comparisons. V2 additionally mentions comparisons with other texture-synthesis methods in the unavailable supplement, without identifying their membership or reporting their results.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the first description of TS aggregation from the average to the maximum of three measurements, although the following paragraph still specifies the average. This is a reported metric revision with ambiguous implementation; the 1,000-caption sample and constraint groupings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The displayed context-window analysis, constraint ablations, and scalability analysis remain unchanged. V2 adds a reference to visual ablations of both constraints in the supplement, but those illustrations are absent, preventing verification of added evidence.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty reporting. The statistical reporting accompanying the retained results is unchanged.

E6.justification: All 60 numerical entries in Table 1 are unchanged, including Tiled Diffusion FID values of 47.9, 48.1, and 50.5. Figure 5 retains its curves, and the qualitative examples remain the same. Results from the newly mentioned supplemental analyses are unavailable for comparison.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 remain unchanged, but replacing average with maximum revises the prose mathematical definition of TS aggregation. The retained average statement makes the revised definition inconsistent. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: flexible tiling across three connection scenarios, two latent-space constraints, the tiling score, and the same applications.

C2.justification: New Section 2.3.2 interprets reuse of a fixed tile set as a time- and space-efficient approach to infinite or panoramic imagery. The existing result interpretations and cross-axis rotation limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The AT description drops the specification that circular padding is applied in the text encoder, UNet, and VAE. This removes a limited implementation detail; Tiled Diffusion's disclosed settings and the code/supplement webpage link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds dedicated texture-synthesis and infinite/panorama subsections and ten references, including MultiDiffusion, SyncDiffusion, DiffCollage, TileGAN, and SeamlessGAN. It also condenses the earlier automated-tiling discussion, substantially broadening the research positioning beyond the original direct competitors.

P1.justification: Section 2 undergoes localized rewriting and subdivision. ITS is renamed CLIP-Score, and short supplementary cross-references are added. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 4, 6, and 7 embed higher-resolution versions of the same examples. Figure 5 and Table 1 replace ITS with CLIP-Score, and Table 1 is compacted. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Broader related-work coverage and higher-resolution figures improve context and presentation. However, v2 introduces conflicting maximum-versus-average definitions of the central TS metric while retaining the reported scores. The additional supplemental evidence is unavailable, so the benefits and loss of evaluation clarity do not establish a reliable net improvement.
